meetings.title: Regular Meeting
meetings.overview: The Council gave a large solar and battery project two more years to get started. It also approved state inmate work crews to help clean up the city, and allowed alcohol sales at two Chamber of Commerce concerts in Main Street Park.
meetings.details:
### What the Council decided
- Approved routine items together, including $775,000 for pavement upkeep, $85,000 for an airport fees study, and $150,000 for shade structures (approved 7-0).
- Supported alcohol sales by the Chamber of Commerce at Main Street Park concerts on November 20 and February 27, and staff will review the park alcohol policy (approved 7-0).
- Gave NextEra Energy two more years to start a solar and battery project on about 2,237 acres (Resolution No. 26-1679) (approved 6-1).
- Gave $42,000 to community groups for fiscal year 2026-2027 (approved).
- Approved a five-year deal for up to 12 low-risk state inmates, paid $1 an hour, to help with city cleanup (approved 6-0, with one Councilmember absent).

### Public comments
- A Support Our Troops Arizona leader invited residents to a Veterans Day golf tournament and auction fundraiser.

### Announcements
- National Night Out is October 14, 5-8 PM, at Main Street Park.
- The Adopt-a-Street cleanup is October 17, 7-10 AM, at Shumway North Park, and the Harvest Festival is October 24 at 6 PM.
- The City's general plan is on the November ballot, with details on the City website.

meetings.title: Regular Meeting
meetings.overview: The Council approved buying an already-equipped police truck for up to $80,000. It also passed an emergency City law letting the Mayor appoint Councilmembers to the short-staffed building appeals board, and accepted an $87,100 grant for the Eloy Fire District.
meetings.details:
### What the Council decided
- Routine items approved together included up to $95,000 to equip two new police trucks and an $87,100 Fire District grant (Resolution No. 26-1678) (approved 7-0).
- The Council approved buying a 2024 Ford F-150 police demonstration truck from San Tan Ford for up to $80,000 (approved 7-0).
- The truck already has most of its emergency gear, will serve a community service officer, and will be paid for with state marijuana tax money.
- A City law change (Ordinance No. 26-1006) lets the Mayor put Councilmembers on the building appeals board as voting members (approved 7-0).
- The board lacks enough members to meet, and staff expect building code appeals soon.
- The change takes effect right away as a temporary fix while the City keeps looking for qualified volunteers.

### Public comments
- A former Maricopa City Councilwoman running for the state House introduced herself and gave the Mayor a challenge coin honoring veterans.

### Announcements
- Sign up online or at the Community Services building for Pizza Palooza (ages 5 to 12, September 18) or a teen painting class (ages 11 to 17, September 25).
- Police will help parents install car seats correctly during National Child Passenger Safety Week, September 20 to 26.
- School fall break starts Thursday, so drivers should watch for children.

meetings.title: Regular Meeting
meetings.overview: The Council approved fixes to clerical errors in four past resolutions, including water and wastewater rate notices. It also passed a new City law letting staff correct such errors and heard that City investments were worth more than $35 million.
meetings.details:
### What the Council decided
- Routine items approved together fixed clerical errors in four past resolutions on water and wastewater rate notices, a fire equipment grant, and a business storage permit (approved 6-0).
- The routine items also included a new City law (Ordinance 26-1005) letting the City Attorney and City Clerk fix clerical errors (approved 6-0).
- The City's investment advisor said City investments were worth more than $35 million on June 30, all in U.S. Treasury investments (no vote).
- The City earned $359,000 from April through June, and a $203,000 paper loss reflected market swings, not money actually lost.

### Public comments
- No one signed up to speak.

### Announcements
- A free outdoor showing of the movie "Michael" is Saturday, August 29, at 7:30 p.m. at Jones Park.
- Reserve vendor spots online for the community yard sale on Saturday, September 5, 6 a.m. to noon, at Main Street Park.
- Filled sandbags are available at Public Works, 1137 West Houser Road, limit six per household (call 520-466-3082).

meetings.title: Regular Meeting
meetings.overview: The Council approved a new $245,811.69 playground for Shumway Park and $99,500 in grants for local groups and events. It also cleared the way to buy land for Sunland Gin Road improvements, using eminent domain only if talks with owners fail.
meetings.details:
### What the Council decided
- The Council approved a new Shumway Park playground for $245,811.69 that doubles the play space and adds an accessible swing and shade (approved 7-0).
- Three groups will share $99,500 in City funding: $71,500 for the Greater Eloy Chamber of Commerce, $25,000 for Corazón de Latinos Unidos for Fiestas Patrias, and $3,000 for the Pinal Hispanic Council for veterans events (approved 7-0).
- The City may buy land and easements to improve Sunland Gin Road and may use eminent domain if owners will not sell (Resolution No. 26-1677, approved 7-0).
- A solar and battery storage project near Milligan Road and South Eleven Mile Corner Road got three more years to start work (Resolution No. 26-1676, approved 6-1, Councilmember Jose Garcia voted no).
- Routine items approved together included a $750,000 sewer cleaning truck, a $120,000 mini excavator, and mapping software costing up to $67,137.60 over three years (approved 7-0).
- The same vote approved a Maverik sign plan at 1120 South Sunshine Boulevard, the July 21 primary election results, and a rules change on fire permits (Ordinance No. 26-1004).

### Public comments
- A resident raised concerns about license plate reader cameras and said some Pinal County cities are dropping them.

### Announcements
- The 75th Eloy Fiestas Patrias is September 11–12, and groups can contact Councilmember JoAnne Galindo to join the parade.
- Residents can send any City question to the new Ask Eloy email, and the Eloy Airpark plan survey is online until August 21.
- Police Chief Sergio Banales shared county data showing community crime cases fell nearly 25% from 2023 to 2025.
